summary: Intermittent 5xx spike correlated with tenant graceful preemption causing request queue polarization
description: Issue summary: Starting 2026-03-10 04:40 UTC Acme AI reported an increase in 5xx errors (502/503) and aborted streaming sessions coincident with scheduled maintenance windows where tenant preemption was active. Impact: multiple customer streaming sessions were disconnected and synchronous API calls returned intermittent 502/503 for ~15-25 minutes at two separate times. Root cause is hypothesized to be interaction between graceful preemption (node retirement) and the ingress prioritizer which caused uneven queue polarization and large head-of-line delays on lower-priority tenant queues, amplifying apigw timeouts and triggering runtime abrupt terminations under CPU pressure.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Deploy two tenant traffic generators: one high-priority and one low-priority tenant (simulate Acme traffic pattern: many short chat streams + small embedding bursts).
2) Trigger graceful preemption on a subset of runtime nodes (simulate node drain via autoscaler scale-in).
3) Observe ingress-prioritizer logs and API gateway metrics while allowing connections to be handoff across runtimes.
4) Watch for queue length imbalance, streaming heartbeat timeouts, and upward 502/503 rates on the low-priority tenant.
Notes: reproduces reliably when preemption window < 60s and when headroom for new worker spin-up is limited.

investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: preemption race causes backlog on the ingress prioritizer.
Evidence: 1) queue_polarization metric spikes exactly at node drain start time; 2) runtime processes show rapid SIGTERM + high CPU and elevated GC/ephemeral thread counts; 3) apigw logs show upstream 502s with proxied latency >10s.
Repro steps validated in staging with scaled-down topology; reproduces when autoscaler scale-in aggressiveness is set to >20% of pool and when prewarm headroom is <2 spare workers per shard.
Temporary mitigation implemented (2026-03-10 05:12 UTC): increased prewarm headroom for affected shard from 1->3 and slowed scale-in throttle for 30m which reduced 5xx to baseline.
Longer-term: engineering action items below.
comments: Maya Chen (Support) - 2026-03-10: Received initial customer report; forwarded logs and graphs to SRE. Escalating to P1 due to streaming session drops.
Arjun Patel (SRE) - 2026-03-10: Confirmed correlation with scheduled node drains. Creating temporary autoscaler config change to increase prewarm headroom; will monitor for 30m.
SRE-Oncall (SRE) - 2026-03-10: Temp mitigation reduced error-rate; still seeing isolated 502s on long-lived streams. Posting runbook link and will attach heap/gc traces if crash persists.
Customer (Acme AI) - 2026-03-10: Noted degraded UX during morning ET hours; asked for ETA on root cause and prevention.
Arjun Patel (SRE) - 2026-03-12: Root-cause analysis in progress. Begin development ticket in runtime to make draining gentler (PR referenced below).
resolution: Mitigation applied: autoscaler prewarm headroom temporarily increased and scale-in throttled for high-priority shards. Rolling patch planned to adjust prioritizer fairness and runtime drain timeout. Customer notified and monitoring is stable at baseline. Follow-up engineering work scheduled.
resolution_notes:
1) Hotfix (config): increase prewarm headroom to 3 and delay aggressive scale-in for 10m windows during maintenance. Implemented 2026-03-10 05:12 UTC.
2) Code fix: runtime PR #1284 adds graceful-drain backoff to avoid SIGTERM until in-flight streams drop below threshold; ingress-prioritizer PR will add smoothing to queue weight adjustments to avoid extreme polarization. Targeted rollout to prod on 2026-03-18 behind canary.
3) Postmortem action: update maintenance runbook to ensure preemption window >= 90s or to schedule tenant-aware drains for dedicated customers.
Customer follow-up: CS emailed remediation summary and timeline; customer requested confirmation once patch is in canary.
